content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Define what a fuel is and explain how fuels release energy
Compare different fuels based on their energy content
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of different fuels
Discuss environmental impacts of burning fuels

is a substance that releases energy when it undergoes combustion. Fuels are essential for transport, heating, electricity generation, and industry. Understanding the chemistry of fuels helps us make informed choices about energy use.
A substance that releases energy in a chemical reaction (usually combustion).
The reaction of a substance with oxygen, releasing heat and light.
Carbon monoxide is toxic (binds to haemoglobin)
= energy released per gram or per mole
Hydrogen has the highest energy per gram but lowest per mole (small molecule).
kJ per gram or per litre
Most H₂ made from fossil fuels
Uses land that could grow food
*Not truly carbon neutral (farming and processing use energy)
These dissolve in rain to form acids
Calculate the energy released when 100 g of methane is burned. (ΔH = -890 kJ/mol)
Compare the energy released per gram for methane and ethanol.
Methane releases almost twice as much energy per gram.
Explain why hydrogen is considered a "clean" fuel.
No carbon dioxide is produced (no carbon in the fuel)
No sulfur dioxide (no sulfur in the fuel)
This is why it's considered clean
Explain why biofuels are described as "carbon neutral".
Plants absorb CO₂ from the atmosphere during photosynthesis
When the biofuel burns, CO₂ is released
The CO₂ released equals the CO₂ absorbed
Net CO₂ change is theoretically zero
(However, growing, harvesting, and processing uses energy, so not completely carbon neutral)
Thinking hydrogen fuel produces no pollution at all
The combustion is clean, but producing hydrogen often uses fossil fuels
Confusing energy per mole with energy per gram
Both measures are useful for different purposes
Limited oxygen causes incomplete combustion (CO and C)
release energy through combustion with oxygen
high energy but non-renewable, produce CO₂
clean burning but hard to store and produce
